question: What primary socio-cultural factor drives the high frequency of injection use in many Nigerian healthcare settings?

options.A: Oral medications are universally unavailable in municipal and rural pharmacies alike.
options.B: Patients frequently believe injections work faster and are more potent than oral medications.
options.C: Intravenous and intramuscular drugs are significantly cheaper to produce and distribute.
options.D: Federal health policies mandate parenteral treatment for all common outpatient diagnoses.

explanation: Community perception heavily influences healthcare-seeking behavior, with many patients demanding injections due to a strong belief in superior efficacy. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T4#GNS122_U3_T4_h1)

question: Which hazardous practice directly contributes to the transmission cycle of blood-borne pathogens in under-resourced clinics?

options.A: Storing multi-dose vaccine vials inside dedicated pharmaceutical refrigerators
options.B: Recapping used needles manually before disposal in puncture-resistant containers
options.C: Washing stainless steel injection trays with warm water and detergent
options.D: Administering intramuscular medications in the ventrogluteal site

explanation: Manual recapping significantly increases the risk of accidental needlestick injuries to healthcare workers and handlers. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T4#GNS122_U3_T4_h1)

question: Which blood-borne virus is known to have the highest infectivity rate following a single percutaneous exposure to contaminated blood?
explanation: Hepatitis B has a high concentration in viral particles and exceptional environmental stability, making its transmission rate following needlestick injury significantly higher than HIV or HCV. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T4#GNS122_U3_T4_h2)

question: Why does parenteral injection bypass primary immunological defenses compared to oral or topical drug routes?

options.A: It permanently neutralizes complement proteins in the systemic circulation.
options.B: It stimulates excessive production of gastric acid that destroys antibodies.
options.C: It introduces pathogens directly past the protective epidermal and mucosal skin barriers.
options.D: It immediately destroys circulating white blood cells within the capillary bed.

explanation: The skin and mucous membranes serve as the primary mechanical barrier against foreign invaders; breaking this barrier via needle insertion directly introduces microbes into internal tissues. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T4#GNS122_U3_T4_h2)

question: What is a major long-term health complication associated with chronic Hepatitis B and Hepatitis C infections?
explanation: Both Hepatitis B and C cause chronic inflammation of the liver, which over years or decades can lead to scarring (cirrhosis) and primary liver cancer. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T4#GNS122_U3_T4_h3)

question: A patient exposed to a contaminated needle months ago presents with fatigue and jaundice. Which characteristic of viral hepatitis explains why they did not seek care immediately after the injection?

options.A: Acute phases of viral hepatitis are frequently asymptomatic or present with vague, non-specific symptoms.
options.B: The incubation period lasts only a few hours, masking the origin of the initial skin puncture.
options.C: Blood-borne viruses temporarily improve immune function before causing sudden organ failure.
options.D: Initial symptoms exclusively affect the skeletal system rather than metabolic pathways.

explanation: Because early symptoms mimic common self-limiting illnesses like malaria or fatigue, infected individuals often remain undiagnosed for long periods. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T4#GNS122_U3_T4_h3)

question: What is the primary clinical feature that distinguishes a deep abscess from simple localized cellulitis following an injection?

options.A: Exclusive involvement of the epidermis without deeper tissue layers
options.B: Presence of a localized collection of purulent fluid requiring drainage
options.C: Total absence of localized pain or tenderness upon palpation
options.D: Immediate resolution of symptoms without medical intervention

explanation: While cellulitis involves diffuse inflammation of skin layers, an abscess forms a distinct pocket of pus (purulent material) that typically necessitates drainage alongside antibiotic therapy. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T4#GNS122_U3_T4_h4)

question: When bacteria from an unsterile injection site enter the systemic circulation, what is the most critical systemic complication that can develop?

options.C: Immediate permanent paralysis of the lower limbs
options.D: Spontaneous regeneration of damaged nerve trunks

explanation: Systemic spread of bacterial toxins and organisms can precipitate severe hypotension and widespread organ failure known as septic shock. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T4#GNS122_U3_T4_h4)

question: Improper anatomical site selection for gluteal intramuscular injections most commonly risks damaging which major nerve?
explanation: The sciatic nerve runs through the lower and inner quadrant of the gluteal region, making improper injections in this area a primary cause of nerve injury and foot drop. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T4#GNS122_U3_T4_h5)

question: A patient receives an intramuscular injection in the buttock and immediately complains of a sharp, electric-shock-like pain shooting down the leg, followed by difficulty lifting the front part of the foot. What complication has most likely occurred?

options.A: Acute viral hepatitis transmission via a shared needle
options.B: Systemic sepsis secondary to bacterial contamination
options.C: Localized subcutaneous cellulitis without deep tissue involvement
options.D: Direct mechanical or chemical injury to the sciatic nerve

explanation: Sharp radiating pain paired with foot drop immediately following a gluteal injection is the classic presentation of sciatic nerve trauma. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T4#GNS122_U3_T4_h5)

question: Why is it essential to document the exact anatomical location and timing of a recent injection during a patient assessment?

options.A: To determine the exact genetic strain of any viral pathogen present in the community
options.B: To help correlate clinical symptoms with specific tissue trauma or localized bacterial introduction
options.C: To ensure the pharmaceutical manufacturing company refunds the cost of the medication
options.D: To eliminate the need for routine baseline laboratory blood investigations

explanation: Knowing when and where an injection was given helps clinicians differentiate between acute inflammatory reactions, nerve trauma, and developing abscesses. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T4#GNS122_U3_T4_h6)

question: Which of the following assessments is most crucial when evaluating an injection site located near a major nerve trunk?

options.A: Measurement of abdominal girth and bowel sounds
options.B: Auscultation of heart murmurs and breath sounds
options.D: Distal sensory and motor function testing

explanation: Assessing movement and feeling distal to the injection site helps identify early nerve impingement or transection. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T4#GNS122_U3_T4_h6)

question: What is a primary nursing responsibility when caring for a patient with a localized injection site abscess awaiting surgical drainage?

options.A: Applying tight compressive bandages to restrict local blood flow
options.B: Administering strong oral laxatives to prevent postoperative complications
options.C: Massaging the fluctuant mass vigorously to promote spontaneous rupture
options.D: Performing sterile dressing changes and monitoring for systemic signs of infection

explanation: Wound care and vigilance for systemic deterioration are core nursing responsibilities in managing localized infections. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T4#GNS122_U3_T4_h7)

question: Why is interprofessional collaboration with physical therapists important in cases of injection-induced nerve damage?

options.A: To perform emergency surgical debridement of necrotic muscle tissue
options.B: To prescribe and administer broad-spectrum intravenous antibiotic regimens
options.C: To implement rehabilitation exercises that prevent contractures and aid functional recovery
options.D: To conduct mandatory serological testing for blood-borne viral loads

explanation: Physical therapy helps maintain joint mobility and muscle tone while nerve regeneration occurs following traumatic injury. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T4#GNS122_U3_T4_h7)

question: What is the most effective engineering control for preventing accidental needlestick injuries in a clinical environment?

options.A: Storing used injection equipment in open utility basins until shift change
options.B: Washing disposable plastic syringes in chemical disinfectant solutions
options.C: Placing rigid, puncture-resistant sharps containers at the immediate point of use
options.D: Requiring clinical staff to recap all used needles using a two-handed technique

explanation: Point-of-use sharps disposal eliminates the hazardous practice of carrying used needles across rooms to discard them. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T4#GNS122_U3_T4_h8)

question: Which of the following practices is strictly contraindicated when handling used injection equipment?

options.A: Wiping rubber drug vial stoppers with alcohol
options.B: Dropping unsecured syringes into a sharps bin
options.C: Manually recapping used needles with both hands
options.D: Wearing clean gloves during medication withdrawal

explanation: Manual recapping is a leading cause of accidental percutaneous injuries and is strictly prohibited under standard safety protocols. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T4#GNS122_U3_T4_h8)
